title: Shifted single-object reduction squares detect actual strict transitions
statement:
Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, a scheme T, and any recorded coefficient-tower datum A of det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian. Let M,N be strict coefficient sheaf towers and s an integer. Given arbitrary level sheaf maps f_n:M_n→N_n, conjugate their shifted degree-zero singles by the canonical exact-evaluation single/shift comparisons to obtain g_n:ev_n(M[0][s])→ev_n(N[0][s]). If every canonical derived reduction square for g commutes, then f_n followed by the actual transition of N equals the actual transition of M followed by scalar restriction of f_m for every m≤n. No local freeness, cartesianness, invertibility of f, or invertibility of l on T is required.

Formal statement:
```lean
theorem shifted_single_reduction_detects_transition
    {l : ℕ} [Fact l.Prime] {E : Type u} [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] {T : Scheme.{t}}
    (A : SpCoefficientTowersAbelian l E T) (M N : spCoefficientTowers l E T) (s : ℤ)
    (f : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (spCoefficientEvaluation l E T A.equivalence n).obj M ⟶
        (spCoefficientEvaluation l E T A.equivalence n).obj N) :
    letI := A.hasDerived
    letI := A.equivalenceAdditive
    letI := A.evaluationLimits
    letI := A.evaluationColimits
    let ev := fun n ↦ (spCoefficientEvaluation l E T A.equivalence n).mapDerivedCategory
    let S := DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (spCoefficientTowers l E T) 0
    let e := fun (P : spCoefficientTowers l E T) (n : ℕ) ↦
      ((ev n).commShiftIso s).app (S.obj P) ≪≫
        (shiftFunctor _ s).mapIso
          (((spCoefficientEvaluation l E T A.equivalence n).mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor
            0).app P)
    let g := fun n ↦ (e M n).hom ≫
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).map (f n))⟦s⟧' ≫ (e N n).inv
    (∀ {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n),
      (systemDerivedTensor A.scalar (spCoefficientCommRings l E T) h).map (g n) ≫
          (A.reduction h).app ((S.obj N)⟦s⟧) =
        (A.reduction h).app ((S.obj M)⟦s⟧) ≫ g m) →
      ∀ {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n),
        f n ≫ (A.equivalence.functor.obj N).transition h =
          (A.equivalence.functor.obj M).transition h ≫
            (systemRestriction (spCoefficientCommRings l E T) h).map (f m)
```

proof.text: Remove the common integer shift using the canonical scalar shift and the exact evaluation shift comparisons. The shift-compatibility theorem identifies the reductions on shifted single objects with the shifted reductions. Cancel the comparison isomorphisms and use faithfulness of the shift functor. This leaves the unshifted derived scalar square.

For each m≤n, transpose the square through the derived adjunction in the supplied SystemScalarModel. Apply A.reduction_rep to degree-zero complexes. The transpose normalization of SystemScalarModel identifies each reduction with localization of the ordinary transpose of A.ordinaryReduction. A.ordinaryReduction_eq identifies that ordinary transpose with the actual strict transition. Naturality of the derived adjunction moves f_n to precomposition and f_m to scalar-restricted postcomposition. Exact restriction commutes with the single embedding. The resulting equality is precisely single(f_n ≫ transition_N) = single(transition_M ≫ Res(f_m)). Only the counit comparison is composed with, never inverted, so arbitrary M and N are allowed, including nonflat coefficient quotients.
Apply faithfulness of the degree-zero single functor to obtain the displayed semilinear transition equation.
